title: Rejections of COVID-19 Support Grant Applications Due To Inability to Produce Retrenchment Letters
what_it_is: Rejections of COVID-19 Support Grant Applications Due To Inability to Produce Retrenchment Letters

sections.label: CSG approvals, rejections, unverified employment
sections.summary: MSF approved the CSG for around 95,000 applicants, rejected about 4,000 whose employment details could not be verified, and does not track rejections for missing retrenchment letters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: As of 20 December 2020, MSF had approved the CSG for around 95,000 applicants, including around 15,000 applicants who received the CSG upon appeal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: There were about 4,000 applicants who were rejected from the CSG as their employment details could not be verified by MSF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: When the applicants do not have supporting documents or CPF records, we would try to contact their employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: However, MSF does not track the number of applicants whose applications were rejected for the specific reason of not being able to produce retrenchment letters from their employers.

sections.label: Involuntary resignation appeals to SSO
sections.summary: Applicants claiming they resigned involuntarily due to employer pressure could appeal to the Social Service Office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Applicants who claim to have resigned involuntarily due to pressure from their employers could appeal to the Social Service Office.

sections.label: CSG closure and CRG launch
sections.summary: CSG applications closed on 31 December 2020, and MSF will launch the COVID-19 Recovery Grant on 18 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Application for the CSG has closed on 31 December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MSF will launch the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG) on 18 January 2021 to support lower to middle income employees and self-employed persons who are financially impacted by COVID-19 in 2021.

sections.label: SSO discretion instead of appeals
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry would give SSOs discretion to process these cases at the frontline without applicants going through an appeal process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Based on that, would the Ministry be open to give the SSOs discretion to process these cases at the frontline, without necessarily having the applicants go through an appeal process, given their bandwidth tax and also the fact many low-wage workers depend on these payouts for some of their basic needs.

sections.label: CSG appeal success rate
sections.summary: 97% of appeals have been successful for the CSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Another number that I would provide is that 97% of appeals have been successful for the CSG.
